items.title: Section: Why the Buddha Taught the Five Aggregates at All — To Show That Nothing About This Body and Mind Is Ever Truly One's Own

items.zh: 又由諸蘊唯有種種名性諸行，當知為顯無我性義，建立諸蘊。
items.en: Second, answering why they were established. Because the aggregates are nothing but a variety of provisionally named conditioned phenomena, one should know that the aggregates were established to reveal the truth of selflessness.

items.zh: 復次，云何色蘊差別？略由六種。一、由事故；

items.title: Section: Form's Six Distinctions Begin — Substance, and Three Kinds of Characteristic Down to the Subtlest Mental Image

items.zh: 二、由相故；三、由識執不執故；四、由識空不空故；五、由想所行故；六、由邊際故。事者，謂所有諸色皆是四大種及四大種所造。相者，略有三種。一、清淨色，二、清淨所取色，三、意所取色。又變礙相是色共相。
items.en:
Second, explaining each; first, substance. Substance names how every form is the four great elements together with what they produce.
Second, characteristic; first, self-characteristic. Characteristic is, in brief, of three kinds: first, pure form; second, form grasped by the pure faculties; third, mind-grasped form.
Second, shared characteristic. The mark of mutability and obstruction remains form's shared characteristic throughout.

items.title: Section: Appropriated Form Versus the World Outside — And the Thief Who Only Ever Saw the Gold

items.zh: 識執不執者，若識依執，名執受色。此復云何？謂識所託，安危事同，和合生長。又此為依，能生諸受。與此相違，非執受色。識空不空者，若識不空，名同分色，由此與識等義轉故。若識空者，名彼同分色，似自相續而隨轉故。
items.en:
Third, appropriated or not; first, appropriated form; first, stating it. Whether consciousness appropriates a given form — whatever consciousness depends upon is called appropriated form. Third, explaining; first, through consciousness's dependence. Consciousness and this form share the same fate of safety and danger, arising and growing together. Second, through generating sensation. This same form, being consciousness's basis, is capable of generating sensation.
Second, non-appropriated form. Whatever is the opposite of this is called non-appropriated form.
Fourth, whether consciousness is engaged or not; first, concordant form. Whether consciousness is engaged or not — when consciousness is not disengaged, this is called concordant form, since faculty and consciousness operate equally upon the same object.
Second, form resembling the concordant. When consciousness is disengaged, this is called form resembling the concordant, since the faculty continues in its own similar continuity regardless.

items.title: Section: Three Ways Perception Takes Hold of Form — Colour Itself, Its Location, and Its Accumulated Shape

items.zh: 想所行者，謂緣色想，略有三種。一者、色想，二、有對想，三、別異想。色想亦三，一、有光影相，二、據方處相，三、積集住相。如是三相，隨其次第三想所行。
items.en:
Fifth, what perception operates upon; first, presenting the kinds; first, perception that takes form as object. Perception operating on form is, in brief, of three kinds: first, perception of colour; second, perception of resistant form; third, perception of differentiation.
Second, the colour-characteristics grasped. Colour's own characteristics are likewise three: first, the characteristic of luminosity and shadow; second, the characteristic of spatial location; third, the characteristic of accumulated configuration.
Second, explaining what is operated upon; first, briefly stating it. These three characteristics, in strict order, are what these three perceptions each operate upon.

items.zh: 取青等相，名為色想。能取行礙，名有對想。能取男、女、舍、田等假，名

items.title: Section: Form's Outer Limit — And the Formless Realm's Own Tears, Fine as Drizzle, at Śāriputra's Passing

items.zh: 別異想。是名想所行差別。邊際者，謂色邊際略有二種。一、墮下界，謂欲廛色；二、墮中界，謂色廛色。當知此中，就業增上所生諸色，說無色界無有諸色，非就勝定自在色說。何以故？由彼勝定於一切色皆得自在，諸定加行令現前故，當知此色名極微細定所生色。
items.en:
Sixth, outer limit; first, presenting its kinds; first, briefly stating it. Outer limit names how form's own limit is, in brief, of two kinds. Second, listing and explaining. First, falling within the lower realm, meaning form bound by the fetters of the desire realm; second, falling within the middle realm, meaning form bound by the fetters of the form realm.
Second, clarifying what has been said; first, stating what this does not mean. One should know that saying the formless realm has no form refers specifically to form generated through the force of ripening karma, not to form manifested through the power of supreme meditative mastery.
Second, explaining why. Why is this so? Because that supreme concentration attains mastery over all form, manifesting it at will through the very application of concentration itself — one should know this form is called the exceedingly subtle form generated by concentration.

items.title: Section: Feeling's Distinctions Begin — Three Self-Characteristics, All Sharing the Single Mark of Suffering

items.zh: 復次，云何受蘊差別？略由五種。一、由事故；二、由相故；三、由生故；四、由觀察故；五、由出離故。事者，謂領納、及順領納法。相者，謂自相及共相。自相有三。樂受、苦受、不苦不樂受。樂受，壞苦故苦；苦受，苦苦故苦；不苦不樂受，行苦故苦。由此因緣，諸所有受皆說名苦。
items.en:
Second, feeling's distinctions; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what are feeling's distinctions? Second, the explanation; first, stating and listing. In brief, there are five: substance, characteristic, arising, contemplation, and liberation.
Second, explaining each; first, substance. Substance names reception together with the conditions that give rise to reception.
Second, characteristic; first, stating it. Characteristic names both self-characteristic and shared characteristic. Second, distinguishing them; first, self-characteristic. Self-characteristic is threefold: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neutral feeling.
Second, shared characteristic; first, revealing its meaning. Pleasant feeling is suffering through the suffering of change; painful feeling is suffering through the suffering inherent in suffering; neutral feeling is suffering through the suffering of formations. For this reason, all feeling whatsoever is said to be suffering.

items.title: Section: Sixteen Kinds of Contact Begin — From the Six Senses Through the Designation-Making Power of Mental Consciousness

items.zh: 是名受共相。生者，謂一切受十六觸所生。何等十六？謂眼觸、耳觸、鼻觸、舌觸、身觸、意觸、有對觸、增語觸、順樂受觸、順苦受觸、順不苦不樂受觸、愛觸、恚觸、明觸、無明觸、非明非無明觸。由所依及所取境故，建立六觸及有對觸。由分別境故，建立增語
items.en:
Second, concluding the name. This is called feeling's shared characteristic.
Third, arising; first, stating it. Arising names how all feeling arises through sixteen kinds of contact. Second, the question raised. What are the sixteen?
Third, listing them. Eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact; resistant contact; designation-generating contact; contact conducive to pleasant, painful, and neutral feeling; craving- and aversion-contact; and clarity-, ignorance-, and neither-clarity-nor-ignorance contact.
Fourth, explaining each; first, the six contacts and resistant contact. The six are established through their respective supporting faculty; resistant contact is established through the object apprehended.
Second, designation-generating contact. This is established through the mental faculty's own discrimination of its object via designation.

items.title: Section: Contact Coloured by Craving, Aversion, or Wisdom — Sixteen Kinds Complete

items.zh: 觸。由領納境故，建立順樂受等觸。由染淨故，建立愛、恚、明、無明、非明非無明觸。是名受生差別。
items.en:
Third, contact conducive to pleasant feeling and the rest. These are established through how the object is received.
Fourth, craving-, aversion-, and the rest. These are established through the mind's own defiled or purified condition.
Fifth, the conclusion. This is called the distinction in how feeling arises.

items.title: Section: The Buddha's Own Eight Questions About Feeling — A Complete Path From Its Arising to Its Final Purification

items.zh: 觀察差別者，一切如來應正等覺出現世間，皆於諸受起八種觀。謂受有幾種？誰為受集？誰是受滅？誰是受集趣行？誰是受滅趣行？誰是受愛味？誰是受過患？誰是受出離？如是觀時，如實了知受有三種，觸集故受集，應知如經分別廣說。如是八種觀察諸受，當知略顯自相觀、現法轉因觀、彼滅觀、後法轉因觀、彼滅觀、彼二轉因觀、彼二轉滅因觀、及清淨觀。
items.en:
Fourth, contemplation; first, the explanation; first, clarifying the contemplation; first, giving rise to it; first, stating it. Every fully and perfectly awakened tathāgata who appears in the world examines feeling through eight kinds of contemplation.
Second, listing them. How many kinds of feeling are there? What gives rise to feeling? What brings feeling to cessation? What is the course of practice leading to the arising of feeling? What is the course of practice leading to the cessation of feeling? What is feeling's alluring taste? What are its dangers? And what is liberation from it?
Second, the resulting realisation. Contemplating in this way, one truly realises that feeling is of three kinds, and that contact gives rise to feeling — as explained in detail in the scriptures.
Second, revealing the condensed meaning. These eight contemplations of feeling should be known, in brief, as: the contemplation of self-characteristic, of the cause of present arising, of its cessation, of the cause of future arising, of its cessation, of the cause sustaining both, of the cause bringing both to cessation, and the contemplation of purification.

items.title: Section: Purification Completes the Eightfold Contemplation — Then Liberation From Feeling, Absorption by Absorption

items.zh: 是名觀察差別。出離者，謂初靜慮出離憂根，第二靜慮出離苦根，第三靜慮出離喜根，第四靜慮出離樂根，於無想界出離捨根。是名出離差別。
items.en:
Second, the conclusion. This is called the distinction of contemplation.
Fifth, liberation; first, the explanation. Liberation names how the first meditative absorption liberates one from the faculty of grief, the second from the faculty of pain, the third from the faculty of joy, the fourth from the faculty of pleasure, and the signless realm liberates one even from the faculty of equanimity.
Second, the conclusion. This is called the distinction of liberation.

items.title: Section: Perception's Distinctions Begin — Its Substance in Language, and a Recap of Its Own Twelve Self-Characteristics

items.zh: 復次，云何想蘊差別？略由五種。一、由事故；二、由相故；三、由顛倒故；四、由無顛倒故；五、由分別故。事者，謂取所緣相及隨順彼法。相者，自相有六種，如前應知。等了相是共相。是名相差別。
items.en:
Third, perception's distinctions; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what are perception's distinctions? Second, the explanation; first, stating and listing. In brief, there are five: substance, characteristic, distortion, freedom from distortion, and discrimination.
Second, explaining each; first, substance. Substance names grasping the object's own characteristic together with the conditions that accord with this.
Second, characteristic; first, the explanation; first, self-characteristic. Characteristic's self-characteristic is of six kinds, as already explained before. Second, shared characteristic. Equally apprehending the object is the shared characteristic. Second, the conclusion. This is called the distinction of characteristic.

blocks.text: The aggregates examined one by one, with a famous line: all feeling, even pleasant feeling, is suffering.

Pure form (the sense faculties) and "form taken by the mind". Master Cháng Bǎi: the second is simply the five sense objects. (Untranslated, 0593c23: the distinctions of the form aggregate are of six kinds, the first by substance.)
Form that consciousness relies on, sharing its safety and danger and growing together with it. Master Cháng Bǎi: consciousness dwells in the body and grows with it.

Of colour, of resistance, and of designated things. Master Cháng Bǎi: perception of colour takes light and shade. (Untranslated, 0594a08: grasping blue and the like is colour-perception; grasping resistance, resistant perception; grasping "man, woman, house, field" and the like, designated perception.)
"No form" in the formless realm refers to karmically produced form, not to the exceedingly subtle form produced by concentration.

Pleasant feeling is suffering through change, painful feeling through suffering itself, neutral feeling through conditioning. Master Cháng Bǎi: pleasant feeling is delightful while it lasts, and painful when it changes.
Mental contact arises through discriminating the object in words. Contact "joined with clarity" is the noble ones' uncontaminated contact, joined with wisdom.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the "way leading to cessation of feeling" is the noble path, which must be practised; he stresses the difference between cessation itself and the path to it.
Each absorption leaves one faculty behind: the third leaves the second's joy, and so on.
"Grasping the object's own mark." Master Cháng Bǎi: grasping marks is the very character of perception.
"Pleasant while it lasts, painful when it changes." The point is not to fear pleasure, but to see clearly what it is.

quiz.q: The English has "purely-grasped form" for 清淨所取色. How does the lecture explain it, and what is the problem?
options: it is suchness grasped by noble ones' pure wisdom, which "purely-grasped" fits well
it is the pure radiance seen in absorption, and should be "luminous form"
it is form taken by mental consciousness, and "grasped" should be "imagined"
it is the five sense-objects taken by pure form, the faculties; "purely-grasped" reads as grasped purely, which is a mistaken rendering
quiz.why: The treatise lists pure form, 清淨所取色, and mind-grasped form. Master Cháng Bǎi: the second is simply the five sense-objects, form, sound, smell, taste, and touch. So 清淨 refers to the pure-form faculties, and the term means "form taken by pure form." The English "purely-grasped form" makes "purely" an adverb describing how form is grasped, which is not the meaning.

quiz.q: What is appropriated form, and what two points does the treatise give?
options: all outer objects taken by consciousness, such as mountains and rivers; and they are what cause it to arise
form born of absorption; and it gives the mind mastery
faculties not working with consciousness; and continuing similarly by their own kind
consciousness relies on it, sharing its safety and danger and growing with it; and on this basis feelings arise
quiz.why: The treatise says appropriated form is what consciousness relies on, sharing safety and danger, growing together, and it is the basis on which feelings arise. Master Cháng Bǎi: consciousness dwells in the physical body and grows with it, and only so does life continue, so form and mind cannot be separated. Mountains, rivers, and plants are not so appropriated and have no feeling.

quiz.q: The English has "discordant form" for 彼同分色. Compared with the lecture, is this rendering suitable?
options: suitable: it is form opposed to consciousness that obstructs it
unsuitable: it is the outer object, and should be "external form"
unsuitable: when consciousness does not work with the faculty, it still continues similarly; it is not discordant, and the English itself goes on to say "similar"
unsuitable: it is the form of the formless realm, and should be "subtle form"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when consciousness does not work with the faculty, the material faculty itself still continues similarly; a faculty working with consciousness on one object is concordant form. So 彼同分 means similar to that concordant form, continuing by its own kind. "Discordant" suggests conflict, which is absent, and the English sentence itself says "in its own similar continuity."

quiz.q: How do the three perceptions of form match the three characteristics?
options: perception of colour takes location; of resistant form, configuration; of differentiation, luminosity
perception of colour takes configuration; of resistant form, luminosity; of differentiation, location
all three take luminosity and shadow, differing only in depth
perception of colour takes luminosity and shadow; perception of resistant form takes location; perception of differentiation takes accumulated configuration
quiz.why: The treatise says these three characteristics are, in strict order, what the three perceptions operate upon. Master Cháng Bǎi spells this out: perception of colour takes the characteristic of luminosity and shadow, perception of resistant form that of spatial location, and perception of differentiation that of accumulated configuration.

quiz.q: If the formless realm has no form, why does the treatise say supreme concentration can manifest form?
options: the treatise contradicts itself, and "no form" should prevail
formless beings still have coarse bodies, invisible to the eye
"no form" refers to form from karma, not to form of meditative mastery, which is called exceedingly subtle form born of absorption
such form is an outsiders' illusion, not real
quiz.why: The treatise clarifies that saying the formless realm has no form refers to form generated by karma, not to form of supreme meditative mastery; this is called exceedingly subtle form generated by concentration. Master Cháng Bǎi: the ripened result of karma for formless beings has no form; the form of those gods is exceedingly subtle form produced through the resolve of absorption.

quiz.q: All feeling is said to be suffering. By which suffering is each of the three?
options: pleasant by the suffering of formations, painful by the suffering of change, neutral by suffering itself
pleasant by suffering itself, painful by formations, neutral by change
pleasant by the suffering of change, painful by suffering itself, neutral by the suffering of formations
all three are suffering itself, with no others
quiz.why: The treatise says pleasant feeling is suffering through change, painful feeling through suffering itself, and neutral feeling through formations; hence all feeling is said to be suffering. Master Cháng Bǎi: pleasant feeling is delightful while present and painful when it decays; neutral feeling, phenomena flowing on ceaselessly, is bound to meet the other two.

quiz.q: Why is one of the sixteen contacts called 增語觸? How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: the sixth uses words to know its object; dependently arisen things have no names, and words are added on
ear-contact arising when sound is loud and words many
words growing as the five take resistant objects
a wholesome contact as speech is strengthened in reciting
quiz.why: The treatise establishes this contact through the discrimination of the object. Master Cháng Bǎi: the sixth consciousness knows its object through words and so gives rise to mental contact; words are language, and dependently arisen phenomena have no words in themselves, so words are added on, whence the name. Resistant contact, by contrast, belongs to the five consciousnesses.

quiz.q: What are clarity-contact, ignorance-contact, and neither-clarity-nor-ignorance contact?
options: clarity-contact is seeing light; ignorance-contact being in the dark; the third being in dimness
clarity-contact is contaminated wholesome contact; the third noble ones' contact; ignorance-contact joined with ignorance
clarity-contact is pleasure; ignorance-contact pain; the third neutral feeling
clarity-contact is noble ones' uncontaminated contact joined with wisdom; the third is contaminated wholesome contact; ignorance-contact is joined with ignorance
quiz.why: The treatise establishes these through defilement and purity. Master Cháng Bǎi: clarity refers to noble ones' contact joined with clarity, an uncontaminated contact joined with wisdom; neither clarity nor ignorance is contaminated wholesome contact, for contaminated good is not evil. Thus the sixteen contacts cover how both ordinary and noble beings meet objects.

quiz.q: The English has "What brings that future arising to cessation?" for 誰是受滅趣行. According to Master Cháng Bǎi, what is 趣行, and what is missing?
options: 趣行 is the practice leading to the stilling of feeling, the conditioned truth of the path; the English does not render path or practice
趣行 is nirvāṇa after feeling ceases, which is unconditioned, so the English is right
趣行 is conduct leading to evil destinies, so the English is reversed
趣行 is the taste of feeling, which the English confuses with its danger
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 趣行 refers to the practice that stills feeling, for one must train in the noble path to still it. He stresses the difference between 受滅 and 受滅趣行, the second being the conditioned path. The English "What brings that future arising to cessation?" conveys a cause of ending but not that this is a path of practice, and it restricts the question to future arising.

quiz.q: Where is each of the five feeling faculties left behind?
options: the first absorption leaves grief, the second pain, the third joy, the fourth pleasure, the signless realm equanimity
the first leaves pain, the second grief, the third pleasure, the fourth joy, and the signless realm leaves equanimity
the first leaves joy, the second pleasure, the third grief, the fourth pain, the signless realm equanimity
all are left at once in the fourth absorption, leaving nothing for the signless realm
quiz.why: The treatise assigns each absorption the faculty left behind there, ending with the signless realm. Master Cháng Bǎi: the third absorption leaves the taste of the second absorption's joy and so leaves the faculty of joy; noble ones accomplishing signless samādhi transcend the fourth absorption's faculty of equanimity.

quiz.q: The substance of perception is grasping the object's mark and what accords with it. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain this?
options: grasping marks belongs to feeling; what accords is pleasure and pain
grasping marks belongs to form; what accords is the four elements
grasping marks is discernment; what accords is six kinds of seeds
grasping marks is perception itself; what accords with it is its conditions, chiefly the habituation of names, phrases, and syllables
quiz.why: The treatise names perception's substance as grasping the object's own mark together with what accords with this. Master Cháng Bǎi: grasping the object's mark is the very character of perception, and what accords with it means the conditions of perception; the habituation of names, phrases, and syllables is its chief condition. This links perception directly to language.
